title: Align embed/rerank pagination edgecases and error norms
creator: Sarah Chen
description: We have observed subtle but customer-visible divergences between the legacy embeddings/rerank endpoints and the unified API adapter around pagination cursor semantics and HTTP error envelopes. This ticket defines an alignment plan to ensure backward compatibility for existing SDKs and client integrations, reduce 4xx/5xx ambiguity, and tame edge cases (empty pages, truncated cursors, and mixed-success responses from partial rerank failures).
background: Multiple support tickets and automated integration tests flagged clients failing during pagination and retry. Examples: client A receives 200 with an empty items array and no cursor, client B receives 204 on expected empty-page semantics, and client C receives 500 with a verbose internal stacktrace rather than a normalized error code. Historically, legacy endpoints returned opaque cursors and a small, inconsistent set of numeric error codes. The unified endpoint introduced standardized envelopes but left a few migration gaps for cursor format, end-of-stream signaling, and retryability metadata.
scope: Formalize a canonical cursor lifecycle and error envelope for embeddings and rerank parity compatibility: 1) explicit end-of-stream indication vs missing cursor, 2) cursor format and versioning header, 3) HTTP status mapping for common client scenarios (rate-limit, validation, partial success, internal failures), and 4) migration shims in the compatibility adapter to accept legacy cursor shapes.
out_of_scope: Changing core model scoring behavior, altering result ranking algorithms, or removing any existing legacy endpoints. This ticket focuses only on API surface semantics and compatibility shim behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical cursor contract documented and published in API reference (examples for empty page, last page, and resumed page)
Compatibility adapter accepts legacy cursor formats and translates to canonical cursor without changing result ordering
HTTP errors normalized to the agreed envelope with stable top-level 'code' and 'retryable' flags
SDK smoke tests (JS/Python) pass against both legacy and unified endpoints with pagination scenarios: single page, multiple pages, empty final page, truncated cursor
proposed_changes: Cursor schema: base64-encoded JSON blob with fields {v: number, type: 'pos'|'token', seq: integer, meta: optional} — adapter must accept legacy base64 opaque tokens and wrap as v:1 migration cursor

End-of-stream semantics: server should return either 'next_cursor': null OR omit next_cursor but include 'end_of_stream': true. Clients encouraged to check both. Adapter will continue to include explicit next_cursor=null for backwards compatibility

HTTP mapping: validation errors => 400, auth => 401/403, rate-limit => 429 with 'Retry-After' header and 'retryable':true in body, partial rerank failure => 206 plus body with 'partial':true and 'failed_ids' list, internal => 500 with non-sensitive short message

Error envelope: {"error_code": "string", "message": "string", "retryable": boolean, "details": [string]} (document as text examples in API reference). IMPORTANT: adapter must strip internal stack traces from responses

Backward compatibility shim: unified endpoint will accept legacy cursors and emit new cursor/version header X-RI-Cursor-Version: v1; adapter will translate legacy cursor -> canonical form and set header
Add a migration header X-RI-Cursor-Supported: legacy,v1 to help clients detect capability and warn in SDKs
Add telemetry tags for each response: pagination_case {single_page,multi_page,last_page,empty_page}, cursor_version_accepted, error_mapping_rule_applied
Document client-side retry best-practices for partial rerank and 206 responses (idempotent retries only for missing segments)
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Spec + small compatibility adapter changes to accept legacy cursors and emit X-RI-Cursor-Version; unit tests added
Phase 2 (1 week): Implement normalized error envelope and HTTP mapping in adapter; SDKs updated to recognize new envelope and migration header
Phase 3 (1 week): Integration test run across JS/Python SDK runners and internal e2e harness; opt-in pilot with 5 existing customers
Phase 4 (1 week): Rollout to 10% traffic with feature flag, monitor telemetry for regressions, expand to 100% if metrics stable
rollout_strategy: Controlled rollout via feature-flagged adapter on the routing layer. Start with non-critical customers and internal teams, then expand. Provide a grace period where both legacy opaque cursor behavior and canonical cursor are emitted to ease SDK upgrades. Publish deprecation timeline for opaque cursor acceptance (12 months after rollout completes).
testing_plan: Unit tests for cursor translation logic (normal and malformed legacy cursors)
Contract tests validating that both endpoints return identical item slices for equivalent cursors
Load test for pagination-heavy workloads to ensure no latency regression due to cursor translation/validation
Integration tests for 206 partial rerank responses and client retry flows
SDK compatibility test matrix across Node 18/20 and Python 3.9/3.11
metrics: pagerror_rate: fraction of pagination API calls returning error per 1000 requests
cursor_mismatch_rate: calls where adapter translated cursor and result ordering differs (target 0)
partial_rerank_rate and partial_retry_success: to monitor 206 cases
open_questions: Do we standardize on next_cursor:null or end_of_stream:true as the canonical signal? (proposal: support both but prefer explicit next_cursor:null)
What exact set of legacy cursor formats must the adapter accept initially? (need ENG input to enumerate known shapes)
Should partial rerank map to 206 with structured 'partial' field or to 200 with warnings? (proposal: 206 to make client handling explicit)
What is the deprecation window for legacy cursor acceptance? (proposal: 12 months with prominent console warnings)
notes: Design reviewed with SDK owners on 2026-02-25; main ask was to emit migration headers to simplify client detection
PM/Support triage 2026-02-03: several customers pinned by pagination regressions after early unified-adapter rollout
Keep error messages user-friendly and non-sensitive. Security to review final error templates before GA
